lines.text: On the second day of the measuring, the wind changed. It blew Tobin's smoke straight out of the square. And it was the children's turn.
Three rings. And this one. Three. Again.
Oswin had taught the grown-ups to groan. Nobody can teach a seven-year-old to be weak. They just bounced up to the table, grinning, and glowed.
Six gifted children, in one little northern village. How remarkable.
The Order honours gifted commoners. These six will come with us to the Academy in Aldcrown. They will be fed, clothed and educated. We leave in three days.
Magister, they're children. They belong with their families.
And the law says gifted commoners belong to the realm, my lord. You know the Charter better than I do. Show me where it says otherwise.
I knew the Charter better than he did. That was the problem. He was right.
That night, half the village crowded into the hall.
We could fight them. Twelve Measurers. We'd be done before supper.
And then the king sends a thousand. And then ten thousand.
Laws are written by men who never had to keep them.
The six children were asleep in the corner. Their parents wouldn't let them out of sight. Ash had curled himself around all six of them, like a wall.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter 24, coming soon.
